description: JSON.string appends one byte at a time (acc <> <<c>>): 35% of decode time on 16,000 log lines. Change lib/json.fz only: count plain bytes up to the next quote or backslash, take the run with <<run :: binary-size(n), r :: binary>>, append once; escapes, control characters and UTF-8 handling unchanged. Spiked: decode 1.64 s -> 1.32 s (-19%), output identical; one 100-character string 406 -> 109 allocations, off-heap bytes 2,970 -> 200; json_decode_cost goldens fall (89 -> 70, 173 -> 114; interp 88 -> 69, 172 -> 113); all JSON fixtures pass on three paths. Patch: scratchpad b183-6/scan_slice.patch. Signal: a fixture pinning off-heap bytes for a long string; goldens lowered. Remove the comment that defers scan-then-slice. Evidence and predictions: proposal page fz-sc8.183.5.html (workspace root); spike files in scratchpad b183-5 and b183-6.
title: The JSON decoder scans a run of plain bytes and slices it once
